A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOTAlign work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and classification experiments, alignment ablations, supervision sweeps and gradient-computation efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds satellite-image and speech retrieval, corruption experiments and hyperparameter sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same linear-teacher stage followed by alignment with supervised SigLIP and unpaired-data KLOT regularization. The corrected main-text gradient already appears correctly in v1's appendix; it does not establish an implementation change. The new modality experiments apply the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds SkyScript satellite-image/text retrieval and LibriSpeech speech/text retrieval, substantially extending the evaluated domains and modalities beyond v1's general image–text benchmarks. It also introduces synthetic-noise scenarios for unpaired embeddings while retaining the earlier dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain their comparator membership and baseline implementations, including Tables 4–6 and Appendix A.2. The added domain experiments reuse previously evaluated CCA, SAIL and STRUCTURE. UOT-RCL is newly cited but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include SkyScript evaluation with 10k/30k test pools, LibriSpeech training with 1k pairs and 100k unpaired samples, weaker-encoder configurations, corruption sweeps and temperature searches using 500 Sinkhorn iterations. Section 6.1 reports teacher epsilon*=0.005, whereas v1 and the retained v2 Appendix A.1 specify 0.01. This leaves the actual default and whether retained experiments were rerun unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds teacher-pair corruption experiments, unpaired Gaussian-noise stress tests, loss-weight sensitivity across supervision/noise levels, and teacher/student temperature sweeps (Appendix B.2). It also adds Sinkhorn convergence analysis and extends encoder-similarity analysis to ResNet-50 and BERT. These substantially expand examination of robustness and design dependencies.

E5.justification: Both versions report spherical sliced Wasserstein distances as means and standard deviations over 20 seeds, using 100,000-sample subsets (v1 Appendix B.4/Figure 12; v2 Appendix B.3/Figure 15). No new run-count disclosure, significance test or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented. Updated correlations are changes in results.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables retain their values, but substantial new results appear. v2 Table 7 reports SOTAlign SkyScript T2I/I2T R@10 of 27.3/27.4 and LibriSpeech S2T/T2S R@1 of 78.4/83.1. Table 8 reports 26.6 COCO MeanR@1 with 50% teacher-pair corruption versus 23.6 for SAIL. Expanded analyses report encoder-similarity correlation 0.95 instead of 0.83 and distribution-shift correlation -0.76 instead of -0.72.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1, Equation 13, corrects the gradient denominator from teacher epsilon* to student epsilon, agreeing with Theorem C.4 and its proof already present in v1. Section 3.3 also corrects projection-matrix dimensions. The appendix's mathematical results and derivations otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain low-supervision alignment using a linear teacher, effective use of unpaired data, efficient KLOT differentiation and robustness across datasets and encoders. The contribution list and conclusion retain their scientific scope; the new experiments provide additional support.

C2.justification: v1 cautions that more encoder-pair observations are needed for firm conclusions; v2 presents mutual k-NN as a reliable diagnostic before alignment. v2 also substantially expands practical interpretations: teacher robustness is attributed to limited linear capacity and OT invariance, mismatched unpaired data are described as producing graceful degradation, and entropy/loss-weight choices receive mechanism-based explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and documents the WavLM-Large speech encoder, corruption construction and additional hyperparameter searches. Most optimizer, architecture, hardware and baseline implementation details in Appendix A remain unchanged. The conflicting teacher-temperature values in Section 6.1 and Appendix A.1 reduce the clarity of the new guidance.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds UOT-RCL as prior OT-based frozen-encoder alignment addressing noisy labels and revises the CLIP background. References for the additional datasets and encoders are added. Positioning relative to OT-CLIP, S-CLIP, SUE and STRUCTURE remains substantially unchanged; the existing Assel/Monge Gap discussion moves from the appendix to Section 5.

P1.justification: Section 6 is reorganized into dedicated design-choice, supervision, data-source, encoder and benchmarking subsections, and Appendix B reorders distribution-shift and benchmarking material. Related work is tightened, local language is corrected, and affiliation/publication text is updated. Much of the existing prose and overall narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the experimental displays with convergence, sensitivity and satellite-retrieval plots plus new Tables 7–8. Distribution-shift and encoder-similarity plots are expanded and redrawn; the latter moves from v1 Appendix Figure 9 to v2 main-text Figure 7. Existing tables and several figures are also redistributed within the revised layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by testing satellite and speech applications and examining teacher corruption, extreme unpaired-data mismatch and tuning sensitivity that v1 did not establish. These additions address important gaps in support for applicability and robustness. The corrected gradient statement and code-access information also help. The new inconsistency between teacher temperatures in Section 6.1 and Appendix A.1 limits reproducibility, but does not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
